manual.engineered_lighting.line2: {0}Deep in the halls of the factories, it can be quite dark. Thankfully, lanterns can help illuminate the machinery.{1}
manual.engineered_lighting.line3: Their light-level can be adjusted by right-clicking them with an Engineer's Screwdriver.
manual.engineered_lighting.line4: {0}Cage lamps are a little more rugged and atmospheric than lanterns, while also providing redstone control. By default, a cage lamp requires a redstone signal to turn on, this behavior can be inverted by sneaking and right-clicking them a screwdriver.
manual.engineered_lighting.line5: {0}Powered Lanterns are one of the first ever invented uses for electric power.{1}
manual.engineered_lighting.line6: To run these, they need to be connected directly to a power grid using LV wires. They will allow power to be transferred through them, allowing multiple of them to be linked in a row.
manual.engineered_lighting.line7: Using the Engineer's Hammer on them will flip them upside down.{0}
manual.engineered_lighting.line8: As long as they are supplied with a little bit of power, they will light up the surrounding area like a normal Lantern, but additionally, they will also prevent hostile mobs to spawn in a 32 block radius!{0}
manual.engineered_lighting.line9: {0}Floodlights are strong lightsources. While they require more power than a simple Powered Lantern, they will create a cone of light up to 32 blocks long.{1}
manual.engineered_lighting.line10: Use an Engineer's Hammer on the top or bottom faces of the block to rotate the light or click its sides to change its pitch.{0}
manual.engineered_lighting.line11: Generally, Floodlights require a redstone signal to run, however their control-behavior can be inverted by right-clicking their base with an Engineer's Screwdriver.
